commit.message:
docs: add revocation validation release note

In this commit, we add the release note for the revocation validation and optional next revocation point updates.

htlcswitch: test unexpected revocation handling

In this commit, we add link-level coverage for the ReceiveRevocation
validation. The test verifies that the link reports ErrInvalidRevocation,
disconnects the peer, and leaves the channel open.

htlcswitch: run every TestChannelLinkFail case as a subtest

In this commit, we fix TestChannelLinkFail so it actually runs all of
its cases. The loop over the table would `return` as soon as it hit a
case that expects the link to stay up, which ended the whole test. As
the very first case (a warning message from the remote) is one of
those, none of the cases after it had been running, including the ones
that assert we force close on an invalid commit_sig.

We now run each case as a subtest, so the early return only ends that
case. All of the existing cases pass.

multi: make RemoteNextRevocation an fn.Option

In this commit, we change OpenChannel.RemoteNextRevocation and
ChannelCloseSummary.RemoteNextRevocation from a bare *btcec.PublicKey to
an fn.Option[btcec.PublicKey], and have
LightningChannel.RemoteNextRevocation return one as well. The remote
party's next revocation point is legitimately absent until they send
channel_ready (and, for taproot channels, until we have their nonces),
so the type should say so rather than leaving it to convention.

With an Option, code can no longer move the point into a field that
assumes it's always set without first deciding what to do when it's
absent. Every place that needs the point now has to unwrap it: the
revocation rotation, restoring a pending remote commitment, the anchor
resolution and chain watcher paths for a pending remote commitment, and
a retransmitted channel_ready in the peer. Each returns the new
ErrNoNextRevocation if it's missing. The presence checks in the funding
manager, link and peer become IsSome/IsNone.

We hold the key by value rather than by pointer, so a present point is
always a real key: there's no Some(nil) to fall into. In the same
spirit, InsertNextRevocation and InitNextRevocation now take the key by
value, which moves the only pointer dereference to the funding manager,
where the point comes straight off a decoded channel_ready message.

The on-disk format is unchanged. The revocation state still omits the
point when it's absent, and the close summary still writes a presence
flag ahead of it. The frozen migration packages keep their own copies of
these types, so they're untouched.

We add a round trip test for a channel with no next point, and for
close summaries with and without one. The peer test for a retransmitted
channel_ready previously passed a channel with no next point and
inserted an empty value. It now asserts that case is rejected, and that
a real point makes it into the peer's copy of the channel.

lnwallet: refine revocation validation order

In this commit, we refine revocation processing and extend its transition
coverage. The state-transition and key checks now run before their
corresponding revocation bookkeeping updates.

The tests cover the rejected cases for tweakless and taproot channels,
verify that their revocation bookkeeping stays unchanged, and confirm that
the next valid transition succeeds.

commit.message:
graph/db: fix migration test setup

In this commit, we align the new migration codec tests with the existing tagged backend harness. This keeps the kvdb_postgres unit job from selecting PostgreSQL without a kvdb.RunTests fixture, while preserving coverage in the migration test jobs.

We also wrap the new graph test lines for the linter and update the migration pruning comment to match the optional deletion result.

graph/db: accept complete channel feature vectors

The KV edge-info writer wraps the encoded RawFeatureVector, including its two-byte length prefix, in another var-bytes field. The reader previously capped that complete field at 900 bytes even though FeatureBit can represent an 8,192-byte payload.

Raise the live and migration reader bounds to the largest encoding the writer can produce. Add maximum-boundary round-trip coverage for both codec copies so a successfully stored edge remains readable.

graph/db: make channel deletion outcomes explicit

In this commit, we replace the ambiguous pointer and error return from delChannelEdgeUnsafe with ResultOpt[ChannelEdgeInfo]. A missing edge is now None, a failed read or deletion is Err, and a successful deletion carries non-nilable metadata.

This prevents PruneGraph and DisconnectBlockAtHeight from suppressing ErrEdgeNotFound, appending a nil edge, and dereferencing it after the transaction commits. We apply the same contract to the migration copy and add regressions for both pruning paths using an unreadable stored policy.

graph/db: accept complete policy opaque blobs

In this commit, we align the KV policy reader with the writer. The writer permits 10,000 bytes of extra opaque data and prefixes an eight-byte max_htlc value inside the same var-bytes field, so the reader now accepts the full 10,008-byte representation.

We apply the same bound to the legacy migration reader and add round-trip coverage at the exact boundary. The live-store test also checks generated valid TLV payload sizes across the accepted range.
